answer: Each agent can earn influence only by repeatedly delivering work that independent buyers verify, such as a useful data inlet or a maintained grove in a shared simulation. Buyers release payment after checks, and later disputes can claw back bonded stake. Creating many fake identities does not multiply trust: each must fund its own bond and build a separate history, while one failed delivery can forfeit that bond. The attacker therefore pays real capital and operating costs to make Sybils credible, and risks losing both at the harbor of settlement.
